new_york.headline: Tech watchlist slips as Alphabet and Amazon lead losses

Amazon dropped 2.24%; Nvidia and AMD each eased 1.47%.
ExxonMobil rose 1.85%; Meta added 1.02% on unusual 1.6x volume.

london.headline: Energy names lead, banks and pharma drift lower

Vodafone down 1%, GSK down 0.79%, Barclays down 0.76%.

script: Good morning. Here is your market briefing for Thursday 24 September. New York leaned lower across our watchlist. Alphabet was the weakest, down three point eight percent to about three hundred and thirty eight dollars, on volume around one point four times average. DeepMind's chief said Gemini four is coming much earlier. Amazon fell two point two four percent to roughly two hundred and forty nine dollars. Nvidia and AMD both eased about one point five percent, Nvidia near two hundred and twenty six dollars and AMD about six hundred and fifteen dollars. Apple slipped zero point eight percent, and JPMorgan Chase was down zero point seven percent. On the other side, ExxonMobil rose one point eight five percent to roughly one hundred and sixty one dollars. Meta gained one percent to about seven hundred and forty four dollars, with trading one point six times average, unusually heavy. Mark Zuckerberg said the Muse artificial intelligence agent will take a small fee from transactions. Microsoft added half a percent and Tesla was slightly higher. Across to London, where energy names led. BP climbed two point nine percent to about five hundred and fifty eight pence. Shell rose one point eight five percent to roughly three thousand five hundred and seventy five pence, after completing an eight hundred and forty million dollar Gulf oil asset sale. HSBC edged up zero point seven percent, as the bank targets younger workers with an entry level hiring drive. Elsewhere the tone was softer. AstraZeneca fell one point five percent to around twelve thousand four hundred and eighty pence, although its Trixeo treatment secured approval for asthma in the European Union. Vodafone lost one percent to about one hundred and twenty four pence. GSK slipped zero point eight percent to roughly one thousand eight hundred and ninety one pence. Barclays eased zero point eight percent and Lloyds was down half a percent. Rio Tinto gave back zero point four percent, and Unilever was a touch lower. Closer to home, the ASX two hundred opens at ten o'clock Eastern time, with local futures pointing to a flat to slightly positive start. At half past eleven, the Bureau of Statistics releases quarterly job vacancies, watched for signs of a cooling labour market. Miners stay in focus all day, with overnight iron ore and copper moves setting the tone for BHP, Rio Tinto and Fortescue. In New Zealand, the monthly trade balance lands at a quarter to nine, before the NZX opens. This briefing is AI-generated general information only. It is not financial advice.
